findings.title: Cleanup removes the literal alias "alias", not the IDPs the test created
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` registers a removal of an IDP named `"alias"`, which never exists. The 20 IDPs created in the loop (`"idp-alias-" + i`) and `idp-alias-20` (line 425) never get removed by these cleanups. Capture the alias, e.g. `String alias = "idp-alias-" + i; ... get(alias)::remove`. Line 425 has the same problem.

findings.title: Changing the shared login predicate also changes the base IdentityProviderBean's federated-IDP list
findings.body: `getLoginPredicate()` is also what `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` returns (services/.../IdentityProviderBean.java:225-227), and `getFederatedIdentityProviders` filters on it (line 213). `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` already adds its own org/public check, so nothing changes there. But the base bean (used when organizations are off) now hides a user's linked IDP if it still has an `organizationId` and isn't `BROKER_PUBLIC`. For example, IDPs that were linked to orgs before the feature was turned off would disappear. If the cache only needs this clause for its invalidation decisions, you could add it to a cache-local predicate and leave the public SPI predicate alone.

findings.title: remove() now always hits the database for the IDP, even when it is cached
findings.body: Before this change, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` ran only when the alias key was invalid. Now it runs on every remove, even when the `else` branch already has `cached.getIdentityProvider()`. You could use the cached model (or `getByAlias`) for the login-invalidation check and only fall back to the delegate when nothing is cached. The cost is small: one extra query per removal.

contracts.action: getForLogin now served from a per-realm, per-FetchMode IdentityProviderListQuery cache
contracts.before_after: Same pattern as getByOrganization: check invalidation, read the revision before the delegate query, addRevisioned, then resolve ids via getById and fall back to the delegate if an id is missing. Unlike getByOrganization it does not check isInvalid(orgId), but org enabled/disabled state is applied at read time by the org-aware wrapper from getById.
contracts.visible_effect: Login page IDP buttons come from cached ids resolved to org-aware models. OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean re-checks isEnabled so IDPs of disabled orgs are filtered.
contracts.failure_mode: If a cached id no longer resolves, the cache key is invalidated and the delegate result is returned, so nothing is lost.

contracts.action: Org link/unlink of an IDP invalidates login caches via update()
contracts.before_after: Linking sets organizationId then calls update. Unlinking clears organizationId and BROKER_PUBLIC then calls update. Both change the organizationId or the predicate result, so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate invalidates all modes. The original model comes from getById as a fresh copy (copy constructor copies the config map), so the caller's mutations don't leak into the original.
contracts.visible_effect: Login page reflects newly linked/unlinked org IDPs after the transaction.

summary:
This PR caches `getForLogin` results per realm and fetch mode. It invalidates that cache when a login-eligible IDP is created, removed or updated, which covers org link and unlink because those go through `update()`. It also re-checks `isEnabled` in the org-aware bean, since cached models are wrapped. The cache and invalidation logic follows the existing `getByOrganization` pattern and looks correct. Organization enable/disable is handled at read time by the wrapper. The new test's arithmetic matches the expected counts.

One fix: the test's cleanup calls register the literal alias "alias" instead of the IDPs it created (lines 381 and 425), so they never clean anything up.

Two things to consider:
- Adding the org/BROKER_PUBLIC clause to the shared `getLoginPredicate()` also changes which linked IDPs the non-org `IdentityProviderBean` shows.
- `remove()` now always queries the database for the IDP, even when it's cached.
